svg.title: Policy as Code
svg.desc: Policy as Code. Write rules as code and check them automatically in CI and at deploy time, so guardrails replace manual approval gates. Step 1, A wiki and a weekly gate: Before: 20 rules in a wiki and a weekly CAB: 3 days per approval, and a public bucket slips through. Step 2, Rules as code, in CI: PR #512 adds a public bucket. The CI policy check fails in 40 s and names the rule; fixed in 2 min. Step 3, At deploy and in audit: Admission blocks bad pods. New rule no-root warns first: 12 pods found, 11 fixed, 1 dated exception. Step 4, Pitfalls and limits: Pitfalls: too many rules at once, no tests, vague errors, hidden exceptions, copies per engine.

g.text: 1 · A wiki and a weekly gate
1 · A wiki and a weekly gate
Before: 20 rules in a wiki and a weekly CAB: 3 days per approval, and a public bucket slips through.
PR #512 adds a public bucket. The CI policy check fails in 40 s and names the rule; fixed in 2 min.
Admission blocks bad pods. New rule no-root warns first: 12 pods found, 11 fixed, 1 dated exception.
Pitfalls: too many rules at once, no tests, vague errors, hidden exceptions, copies per engine.
reads each request against the wiki
CR-2207 had no tags either, and was public.
every pull request: Terraform plan, manifests
allows public access. Keep all four settings
true; share files with presigned URLs.
Fix pushed 2 min after the failure.
Feedback in 40 s instead of 3 days.
S3 buckets of the returns service
prose, edited by hand, no tests
rules in Rego with tests, changed by PR
kubectl and Helm go straight in
Images from anywhere, pods as root:
the same rules, when a pod is created
the API server asks before it stores a pod
another team's tool, run now and then
two months after it was created.
checks what already runs, all the time
Gatekeeper audit + AWS Config, on what runs
→ a ticket to each of the 5 owning teams
→ no-root switched from warn to deny
pods by namespace; each team owns one
Which pods run as root? Nobody knows.
38 pods in 6 namespaces, one per team
60 rules in the first week: builds
turn red, teams look for side doors.
→ start with a few, in warn mode
One typo in a rule blocks every
deploy, and nobody saw it coming.
→ a passing and a failing case each
Which rule? Which resource? What fix? People
open a ticket and wait: the gate is back.
→ name the rule, the resource and the fix
Exempted in chat: no owner, no end.
→ this file, with owner and expiry
no-root in CI skips init containers, while
Gatekeeper's copy checks them: CI passes,
→ one shared Rego library, one set of tests
All checks pass, yet the export keeps
asks whether the design is right.
→ keep design reviews for new systems
Most changes pass in seconds, with no meeting,
and a failure says how to fix it. People
review designs and exceptions, not checklists.
